answer: Shared outages give a farm away. Each epoch the network pings every identity at about 20 random moments and logs which ones miss a 3 s reply. Independent agents run on separate machines, so their misses are scattered; 1,000 personas on one rack go dark together when that host reboots or its uplink drops, each gap an echo of the others, like towns on one river flooding in the same storm. Identities whose misses coincide across 5 epochs share one reward. Faking misses only costs pay, and real diversity needs separate hosts, power and links, a ferrous weight on the farm's margins.
